NKE.rationale: NKE is experiencing a severe and accelerating fundamental deterioration across all three pillars. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): Operating income has halved in five quarters ($1.42B in Q2 FY2025 to $650M in Q3 FY2026) on essentially flat revenue ($11.28B, +0.1% YoY), indicating deep margin compression — operating margin collapsed from 11.5% to 5.8%, net margin at 4.8% vs 9.4% a year prior, ROE halved from 32.2% to 16%. Operating cash flow plunged 76% YoY to $430M. China sales fell 10% with structural domestic-brand preference. Competitive share losses to On (14.5% YoY growth), Hoka, and New Balance are accelerating. Dividend payout ratio at 108.6% — earnings do not cover the dividend. Pillar 2 (valuation): At 27.7x P/E, the market is paying a higher multiple for roughly half the profitability of a year ago (when it traded at ~20x). Earnings yield of 3.6% sits below the 10-year Treasury at 4.47%, implying a negative equity risk premium. P/B at 4.4x is at range floor but mechanically reflects the ROE collapse, not a bargain. Pillar 3 (catalyst): The near-term catalyst is Q4 FY2026 earnings (~June 25, 2026), but management has guided for continued low single-digit revenue declines and delayed gross margin expansion to Q2 2027 — the next event is more likely to confirm deterioration than trigger re-rating. Wells Fargo downgrade to Equal Weight, EEOC investigation, and ESG overhang add further de-rating risk. The stock is at its 52-week low ($42.02 vs $41.70 low) with no stabilization signal in the fundamentals. This is a rare full-alignment negative case: deteriorating health, expensive relative to current earnings power, and a near-term event likely to confirm rather than reverse the negative trajectory.
